title: Phase separation control of transcription in Ewing sarcoma
text:
This project seeks to understand the role of EWSR1 to participate in the activity of a fusion protein,
EWS-FLI1, and drive Ewing sarcoma development by involving a process known as phase
separation, creating a semi-stable molecular scaffold. Our working model is that these molecular
scaffolds localize the machinery for transcription to active genes and aberrant molecular scaffolds
introduced by the EWS-FLI1 fusion can titrate away EWSR1 activity. This proposal uses a
proteomics, genomics, and biochemical approaches to investigate the ability of EWS-FLI1 to redirect
EWSR1 activity in the cell.

title: Multiscale Modeling of Enzymatic Reactions and Bioimaging Probes
text:
This project aims to develop quantum-mechanics-based multiscale computational
methods to quickly and accurately model enzymatic reactions and biomedical imaging
probes. It will lead to reliable and efficient computational tools for use by the general
scientific community. It will facilitate the study of enzymatic reaction mechanisms and the
computer-aided design of new bioimaging probes.

title: Investigating Neuro-Immune Regulation by Gut Fungi
text:
Millions of Americans suffer from inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), a condition marked by intestinal
inflammation and abdominal pain, and emerging research indicates the gut fungal mycobiome may be a
contributing factor in this disease. Our research aims to investigate if fungi in the gut promote
inflammation-associated pain and determine the roles of candidalysin and cytokine signaling in neuronal
activation and pain modulation in states of gut inflammation.

title: Investigating the role of Wnt signaling effectors on the neuron-glia switch and OPC specification during development and after injury.
text:
The neuron-glia switch orchestrating sequential production of neurons and glia from distinct neural progenitors
is essential for functional nervous system development and successful regeneration after injury. This proposal
aims to identify how factors modulate Wnt signaling to regulate the neuron-glia switch and drive gliogenesis in
neural progenitor cells during development and following spinal cord injury. The proposed experiments will
provide insight into the molecular mediators of neural progenitor specification and emphasize the importance of
the neuron-glia switch during development and after injury.

title: Core 1- Expression and Molecular Biology (EMB) Core
text:
NARRATIVE, CORE 1: EXPRESSION AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY (EMB) CORE
The EMB Core addresses a key challenge for SBDR6: limited high-quality protein samples. It will provide
centralized resources and expertise in advanced recombinant protein expression, analyze endogenous DDR
proteins using CRISPR-KI engineered cell lines, and support anaerobic purification of oxygen-sensitive proteins.
This synergy with Projects and the SCB Core will expedite SBDR research, enabling deeper mechanistic insights
into challenging DDR proteins and assemblies.

title: Interdisciplinary Biomedical Imaging Training Program
text:
Relevance to Public Health. Biomedical imaging enables early disease detection, assessment of therapy,
and minimally invasive treatment of disease. Especially with the advent of cellular and molecular imaging and
machine/deep learning, biomedical imaging research requires persons with strong interdisciplinary training.

title: SoS:BIO How Artificial Intelligence Shapes Science: Evidence from Structural Biology
text:
RELEVANCE (See instructions):
Protein structures are central to understanding disease and designing drugs, but determining them
experimentally has historically been slow and costly. AlphaFold2 has made predicted structures available
for virtually every known protein, potentially transforming biomedical research and drug discovery. This
project provides rigorous causal evidence on whether this Al breakthrough is accelerating health-relevant
science.

title: Scalable, single-molecule and single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling in primary immune cells
text:
Current short-read sequencing methods (and associated single cell applications thereof) are insufficient
for studying the chromatin architecture and sequence of complex genomic regions of key importance for
immunology, such as HLA and T- and B-cell receptor loci. Further, existing methods still lack the sensitivity to
capture data from rare cell types in mixed populations without exorbitantly large sample inputs. Here, EpiCypher
is collaborating with Dr. Stergachis of the University of Washington to develop a multiomic platform that leverages
long-read sequencing and DNA amplification for the simultaneous detection and analysis of DNA sequence,
chromatin structure, and protein binding at single molecule resolution from heterogeneous cell populations.

title: Synaptic basis of temporal learning in the cerebellum
text:
In this application, we propose an ambitious research program aimed at a mechanistic understanding of whether
neural circuits harness rapid changes in synaptic strength to sculpt neural dynamics to learn temporal temporally
precise motor behaviors. The cerebellar cortex is a simple circuit amenable to detailed monitoring of its synaptic
and neuronal activity and known for controlling temporally precise behaviors. Deficits in cerebellar function can
lead to ataxias, autism spectrum disorders, and psychiatric disorders.

title: Nanobodies for Dissecting the Structure and Function of Oligomeric BAX
text:
BCL-2 family proteins are essential arbiters of programmed cell death during development and homeostasis and
when deregulated contribute to the development, maintenance, and chemoresistance of human cancers. A
critical missing link in our understanding of the apoptotic pathway is how BAX, an essential executioner protein,
self-assembles into higher-order oligomers to permeabilize the mitochondrial outer membrane. The goal of my
research is to harness cutting-edge nanobody technology and the first homogeneous species of oligomeric BAX
to provide new structural insight into the execution phase of BAX-mediated apoptosis and thereby inform new
opportunities to modulate BAX for therapeutic benefit in cancer.

title: Role of the L1 retrotransposon in interferon-positive SLE
text:
This new projects will explore the role of the Long Interspersed Nuclear Element-1 (LINE-1, or
L1) in type I interferon-mediated SLE. We will continue to characterize autoantibodies against
L1-encoded proteins, ask how early in the disease they appear, how L1 transcription is
upregulated in SLE, which cells that express it, and if the L1 expressing cells also contain
reverse-transcribed RNA and interferon beta. Finally, we will test inhibitors of L1 reverse
transcriptase in these cells.

title: Frugal Science Academy: Training K-12 innovators and democratizing synthetic biology tools
text: This project develops low-cost laboratory tools, teaching materials, and professional development that help high school teachers bring hands-on synthetic and molecular biology activities into school classrooms. Improving access to practical biotechnology instruction can strengthen science education and preparation for future work in areas relevant to biomedical research and public health.

title: Neuromodulation of sex-specific behaviors
text:
Many brain disorders show sex differences, but the mechanisms are unclear. This project utilizes C. elegans to
investigate how neuropeptides, the brain’s signaling molecules, differentially tune the same circuits in females
and males, laying the groundwork for more personalized brain health strategies. This project offers mentored,
hands-on research opportunities for undergraduates, developing technical, analytical, and communication skills
while strengthening the NIH-aligned biomedical workforce.

title: Emerging Flea-Borne Rickettsial Diseases: vector competence and transmission biology
text:
Rickettsioses are diseases caused by bacterial pathogens belonging to the genus Rickettsia.
Pathogenic Rickettsia are typically transmitted to humans by blood-feeding arthropods (insects and ticks).
This project seeks to examine the interplay between Rickettsia felis and the vector fleas, to better
understand the epidemiology of an emerging flea-borne rickettsiosis.

title: Pharmaceutical Sciences and Pharmacogenomics
text: The current study will shed mechanistic light into understanding the role of fibroblast growth factor 15 and 19 (FGF15/19), mainly induced by farnesoid X receptor in the small intestine by bile acids, in regulating drug metabolizing enzyme gene expression and activating a xenobiotic nuclear receptor, constitutive androstane receptor, to regulate liver drug metabolism. Activation of xenobiotic nuclear receptors by gut-derived endocrine factors is significant and novel. This knowledge will shed light in designing new and safe medicines to treat liver diseases, including MASH, while preventing adverse effects and drug-drug interactions.

title: Precision Liver Cancer Modeling by CRISPR Editing of Primary Human Hepatocytes
text:
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the most common type of liver cancer, is an aggressive disease with limited
therapeutic options and poor prognosis. Progress in developing effective targeted therapies for HCC has been
hampered by the limitations of existing preclinical models. This proposal aims to develop a versatile modeling
platform that can recapitulate HCC molecular heterogeneity through defined gene alterations, providing unique
and valuable tools for the discovery of new therapies that improve patient outcomes.

title: Novel wearable sensor calibration and validation for automated measurement of screen time in children
text:
The accurate assessment of digital media use in children is essential for the development of evidence-based
screen use guidelines. We aim to validate wearable light sensors using advanced analytics and data processing
in both laboratory and naturalistic settings, thus providing an objective, scalable method to assess children’s
screen media use.

title: Automated Assessment for Robotic Suturing Utilizing Deep Learning Algorithms
text:
Surgical performance directly impacts patient outcomes. Prostate cancer, the most common
cancer in men, is treated with surgery (robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP)) that can
lead to impotence, incontinence, and even death. Reliable means of objectively assessing
robotic surgical skills are required. The proposed work will automate technical skills
assessment, empowering surgeons with valuable knowledge to minimize prostatectomy surgical
risk.

title: Physical, cellular, and molecular control of tissue fission and fusion
text:
During embryonic development, tissues split and merge to generate organs. The goal of this project is to dissect
the mechanics of how cells within a tissue rearrange to split and how cells from different tissues interact to merge
using the formation of a mechano-sensory organ called neuromast in zebrafish as a model. Our findings will
improve understanding of organ malformation and inform the future development of therapeutic strategies
against such birth defects.

title: Peeling Back the Layers of Mitochondrial Aging
text:
Mitochondria have long been appreciated to play a critical role in the development of the biology of aging, yet
our understanding of the role of mitochondria in aging remains simplistic in many ways. Therefore, this proposal
will expand our understanding of how mitochondria regulate aging by investigating how functionally distinct intra-
and intercellular mitochondrial subpopulations change throughout life and influence aging. This work is relevant
to public health because it will develop a basic science understanding of aging that will pave the path toward
development of new therapies to combat age-dependent disease.
